transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Um, well, I came in because... people have been noticing how I'm moving lately, and I guess I've noticed it too. 

It's kind of weird. Sometimes they can actually see me moving like I'm underwater, you know? Just taking forever to answer a question or even just to get out of a chair. And then, other times, it's the exact opposite. I'll just be pacing around my apartment and rubbing my hands together... kind of like I'm trying to shake off a really bad call from work. It's just very noticeable, so I figured I should come in and talk to someone about it.
Have you been hearing voices that other people do not hear?

Yeah, I actually have. Um, it's usually stuff from work. I’ll hear my old headset beep, or like... a supervisor-type voice will just say my name out of nowhere. Sometimes it tells me I'm being too slow. The thing is, my laptop is completely closed when this happens, and there’s no phone ringing at all. So, yeah, I am hearing things that aren't really there.
Have you been feeling unusually elevated or irritable lately?

No, not really. I haven't felt elevated or... hyper, I guess. And I wouldn't say I've been unusually irritable either. I mean, I get a little frustrated with work stuff sometimes, but nothing extreme or out of the ordinary. So, no, I haven't really noticed feeling like that.
Have you been feeling persistently sad or hopeless lately?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or hopeless. I mean, things are a little stressful, but I don't feel down in the dumps or anything like that. Just kind of... normal, mostly, aside from the other stuff I mentioned.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical or neurological condition that might explain these changes in your movements?
No, I haven't. Um, I don't have any medical conditions or neurological issues that I know of. I've never been diagnosed with anything like that.
Did these movement changes begin after you had a significant medical illness?
No, they didn't. I haven't had any major illnesses recently, or really ever. So it definitely didn't start after being sick.
During the times when you move very slowly, do you ever become completely unable to move or speak?"

No, I wouldn't say I'm completely unable to move or speak. It's not like I'm totally paralyzed. It's more like... well, when I get overwhelmed, I sometimes catch myself just getting stuck in the middle of doing something. Like, I'll be standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug halfway to my mouth, just paused there. Or I'll end up walking the same little loop by the couch over and over for no real reason. So I can still move, it's just kind of getting stuck on pause for a bit.
How long have you been hearing these voices?

Um, I'd say it's been about a year and eight months now. The voices, and... well, those feelings I have about being tracked, they've both been around for that long. And it's not just when the sadness gets really bad, either. They've been happening even when I'm not in the middle of a really low period.
When you become stuck in a position, can someone else move your arms or legs into a different position, and do they stay there?

No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody has ever tried to move my arms or legs when I get stuck like that, so I can't say for sure. But I don't feel like I'm locked in place or anything. It's just a pause. I'm sure if someone nudged me or tried to move my arm, I'd just snap out of it and move normally again.
Have you had periods lasting several hours when you barely move or speak and do not respond to people around you?

No, it's never been like that. I've never had a time where I just sit there for hours ignoring people or not moving. Like I said, it's just quick little moments where I pause, but I'm still aware of what's going on around me. If someone talked to me, I'd definitely respond.
